newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch in quandary over mass Tamil asylum flight.
newsitem.headline: Dutch in quandary over mass Tamil asylum flight.

text.p: A chartered aircraft carrying 173 Sri Lankan Tamils made an unauthorised landing at Amsterdam's Schipol airport on Sunday, leaving the Dutch in a quandary over their policy towards refugees from the troubled island.

Dutch NOS television news said a Turkmenistan Airlines Boeing 757 had flown to Schipol without the permission of Dutch aviation authorities and its Tamil passengers had destroyed their travel documents and claimed asylum.
There have been no reports that the crew were forced to fly the aircraft to the Netherlands.

The Dutch justice ministry confirmed that all the Tamils had requested asylum and would be allowed to stay while their requests were processed. The majority have already been taken to reception centres, it said.
The Dutch courts have stipulated that anyone from Sri Lanka who applies for asylum is entitled to a full hearing process, which can take years to complete.
"Dutch judges have decided that Sri Lanka is not a country to which you can simply return Tamils, and perhaps they had got to hear that," advocate J.Hofdijk told the NOS.
"I understand that our neighbouring countries take a rather less sympathetic attitude and, well, you would tend to go where you were safer."

The Sri Lankan government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in a 14-year war for independence by minority Tamils in the north and east of the island. Tamil groups say the toll is much higher.
Dutch aviation authorities were adamant that the flight had not had permission to fly to the Netherlands. It is thought to have taken off from the Turkmen capital Ashgabat.
On initially receiving a flight plan from the airline, they had requested more information, a spokesman told the NOS.
"This was not answered and that means very explicitly that we gave them no permission to fly here, and they did anyway. We are very angry about that," he said.
The justice ministry said the Turkmen airliner was still at Schipol on Monday night and had been forbidden to leave. The crew were being questioned.
